page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-megamem-56 is a dedicated virtual machine instance belonging to the Network Optimized server family. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, the server provides 56 dedicated vCPUs paired with 744.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a high memory density of 13.29 GB of RAM per virtual processor core. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Resource allocation relies entirely on dedicated vCPUs, preventing compute contention from shared hypervisor tenants. Because local storage is absent, persistent data structures and root operating system volumes must rely on network-attached storage infrastructure. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring network address translation or allocated external IPs for direct outbound and inbound internet routing.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the large memory-to-vCPU allocation allows operations to scale large resident data sets without provisioning unneeded processor cores. This profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including enterprise in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, SAP HANA instances, and memory-heavy transactional processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-megamem-56 is an x86_64 virtual machine within the Network Optimized server family, configured with 56 dedicated vCPUs and 744.0 GB of system RAM. This configuration provides a high memory density of 13.29 GB per virtual processor core, catering directly to memory-bound enterprise software stacks. The machine includes no onboard local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistent data retention, and features no hardware GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Compute allocation is fully dedicated to ensure stable CPU execution without noisy-neighbor interference. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the m4n-megamem-56 delivers resource efficiency for operations that require extensive memory footprints without demanding matching compute scaling. The server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching tiers, and high-throughput transactional database management systems.
